title: Inheritance and Verdict Revisited
premise: Tamsin Villalobos, a night-shift taxi dispatcher whose hobby of unpicking 'accidental' deaths has quietly solved three cases, receives an anonymous retainer to prove that wealthy matriarch Odile Ferrant will NOT be murdered before her inheritance trial begins. When Odile dies anyway — on schedule, in a way only someone with access to the sealed case file could have staged — Tamsin realizes her client hired her not to prevent the murder but to witness it, making her either alibi or scapegoat. As the trial clock ticks down, she discovers the killer is the one person who helped her solve her first three cases: her old mentor, retired detective Ambrose Kettle, who has been laundering his crimes through her deductions for years. In the courtroom's shadow, Tamsin turns the mentor's own file-obsessed methods against him, baiting a confession recorded live as the verdict is read.
about_author: Marguerite Lockridge spent a decade answering phones for a regional cab company before turning the voices in her headset into fiction. She writes mysteries from a converted dispatch booth in coastal Maine, where she still keeps the night hours.

chapters.title: The Retainer
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. On a slow night shift, a lawyer's courier delivers a cash retainer and a single instruction: prove Odile Ferrant will not be murdered before her trial. Tamsin's instinct says the phrasing is wrong — you don't pay to prove a negative. Emotional beat: wary curiosity sharpening into unease as she pockets money she probably shouldn't.

chapters.title: House of Ferrant
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. She surveils the Ferrant estate from a cab parked across the road, cataloguing heirs: a resentful son, a second wife, a caretaker nephew, and Odile herself, sharp-tongued and unafraid. Emotional beat: Tamsin recognizing the family's fear is real even if the danger's shape isn't yet.

chapters.title: Three Accidents
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV, with flashback texture. She reviews how she solved her three prior deaths — a fall, a drowning, a garage fire — and the method she shares with someone: her old mentor Ambrose Kettle, who taught her to read case files like sheet music. Emotional beat: nostalgia laced with pride, planting the mentor bond readers will later dread.

chapters.title: A Call at 3 A.M.
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Odile Ferrant herself calls the dispatch line, asking for a ride and instead asking Tamsin who paid her. Odile knows about the retainer; she suspects her own family and wants an outsider watching. Emotional beat: two wary women forming an alliance neither fully trusts.

chapters.title: The Sealed File
chapters.summary: Ambrose's POV (first shift away from Tamsin). The retired detective reads a court-sealed evidence summary he should no longer possess, annotating it with unsettling precision. He makes a phone call we don't hear the answer to. Emotional beat: quiet menace disguised as routine competence.

chapters.title: Dead on Schedule
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Odile is found dead in her locked conservatory — exactly the manner, exactly the window, the retainer described. Police call it heart failure. Tamsin knows better: the details match a scenario only someone with the sealed file could construct. Emotional beat: horror curdling into guilt — she was paid to prevent this and failed.

chapters.title: Person of Interest
chapters.summary: Detective Reyes's POV. The lead investigator pulls Tamsin's history with unsolved deaths and finds it suspicious rather than helpful. Interview scene crackles with mutual sizing-up. Emotional beat: Tamsin realizing the trap around her is tightening from both sides — killer and law.

chapters.title: What the Client Bought
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. She traces the retainer's money through shell accounts and finds it originates inside the Ferrant estate — meaning a family member paid to stage-manage the death's aftermath, with her as witness. Emotional beat: cold fury replacing self-doubt; she stops being prey and starts hunting.

chapters.title: The Nephew's Alibi
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Caretaker nephew Julian Ferrant has an airtight alibi — too airtight, timestamped by a taxi Tamsin herself dispatched. Someone used her own system to build innocence. Emotional beat: violation and vertigo; the killer has been inside her world for weeks.

chapters.title: Mentor's Counsel
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Tamsin brings the case to Ambrose, who dissects it brilliantly while steering her toward Julian. Interleaved with Ambrose's private chapter: he planted the trail. Emotional beat: warmth on the surface, dramatic irony underneath — readers see what Tamsin can't.

chapters.title: Second Wife, First Lie
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Marisol Ferrant admits Odile was changing her will and had scheduled a meeting with a forensic accountant — motive for every heir. But Marisol's lie about her whereabouts cracks under Tamsin's timeline work. Emotional beat: the satisfaction of deduction shadowed by the knowledge that any suspect could be a decoy.

chapters.title: The Pattern Across Cases
chapters.summary: Detective Reyes's POV. Reyes independently reopens Tamsin's three solved deaths and finds each had a consultant's fingerprints in the record — advice given anonymously through letters signed 'K.' Emotional beat: dawning institutional suspicion aimed at the wrong target, raising stakes for Tamsin.

chapters.title: Trial Date Set
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. The inheritance trial begins; the will contest becomes a public theater where the murder question shadows every testimony. Tamsin attends, recognized, photographed. Emotional beat: claustrophobia — the deadline from the blurb now literal, days remaining.

chapters.title: Break-In at the Booth
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Her dispatch office is searched overnight; her files on all four deaths are copied, and a page from Odile's own notes is left behind like a taunt. Emotional beat: fear transmuting into certainty — the killer needs her, which means she has leverage.

chapters.title: The Accountant's Ghost
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. She finds the forensic accountant Odile meant to hire — alive, hiding, holding Odile's dossier alleging decades of embezzlement funneled through... a police pension fund. Emotional beat: the ground shifting; the motive points beyond the family entirely.

chapters.title: Letters Signed K
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Cross-referencing the anonymous 'K' letters against Ambrose's handwriting habits, she confronts the unbearable arithmetic: her mentor authored the advice that cracked her first three cases — and staged them. Emotional beat: grief and betrayal, the novel's emotional core.

chapters.title: Confession by Proxy
chapters.summary: Ambrose's POV. He explains himself to a mirror-calm degree: he killed to test minds worthy of his method, and Tamsin was his finest instrument. He offers her partnership or ruin — she's now entangled enough to hang beside him. Emotional beat: seductive menace; the reader feels the pull Tamsin must resist.

chapters.title: Setting the Trap
chapters.summary: Tamsin and Reyes's POV, alternating. Uneasy allies now, they build a sting: feed Ambrose a falsified file detail only he would act on, timed to the trial's final day when he must silence the accountant. Emotional beat: tense collaboration, trust built deliberately where it once grew by accident.

chapters.title: Verdict Day
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. The jury returns on the will contest as Ambrose moves on the accountant in the courthouse annex. Tamsin springs the trap, recording his confession as he walks her through, step by step, how he'd have gotten away with all four. Emotional beat: climax — terror, clarity, and the discipline to let him talk.

chapters.title: The Arrest
chapters.summary: Reyes's POV. Ambrose nearly turns the tables, invoking privilege and procedure, until the recorded confession plus the pension-fund paper trail close every exit. His last look at Tamsin is almost proud. Emotional beat: catharsis without triumph; justice arrives but costs something.

chapters.title: What She Owes the Dead
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Aftermath: the Ferrant will upheld, Julian cleared, Marisol's small lies forgiven, and Tamsin formally thanked by a police force that once eyed her. She declines their job offer. Emotional beat: quiet reckoning with loyalty — hers to Ambrose, and to truth, and which won.

chapters.title: Night Shift
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV, final scene. Back at the dispatch board, phones blinking, she takes a call from a stranger with a voice like a held breath: another death that wasn't an accident. She reaches for a pen. Emotional beat: resolution with a door left open — the work continues, and so does she.
